note: Figures for the IPB pages of the Ground Guide's Extended View (IPB_Plan.md). Every figure has a basis: D = read from a pamphlet or manual (cited), T = typical public figure (to confirm), E = my estimate or proposal (to confirm), U = the user's decision. Figures are implemented exactly as written in the source, conflicts noted, never 'corrected' (user, 2026-11-14).
handling: The D figures are numbers read from restricted Pakistan Army pamphlets (C&SC Quetta IPB book; Desert Warfare; Mountain Warfare; Operations of War Vol I and II; Infantry Battalion in Battle; The Rifle Company, Platoon and Section in Battle). Keep this file under the same handling terms as those pamphlets before it goes outside the owner's own systems.

basisCodes.E: my estimate or proposal, to confirm

decisions.goingRule: The IPB coding uses the IPB book's criteria only; GROTBC keeps its own card and enforce rule. A criterion the bundle cannot test is reported as not assessed, never filled in from GROTBC.
decisions.proformaGroups: Two groups of A B C D with blank, user-named headings (the book leaves them blank, p 21).
decisions.communications: Row h of the proforma is two lines: Rds & LOC, and Sigs.
decisions.mcWidthsAllForces: The corridor widths and spacing serve all forces: ATP Table 4-2 gives the same figures for a mechanized force.
decisions.goSlope: GO slope is 'less than 30 degrees' as written (IPB p 11); SLOW-GO 30-45 % and NO-GO 45 % or more uphill, in percent as written. Where they overlap uphill the stricter class wins.
decisions.avlbSpan: Not known: a setting, default 18 m (basis T).
decisions.attack: Frontal attack is dangerous with small chances of success; a flanking attack that chokes the enemy MSR is encouraged; Left or Right by weighing the factors.

coding.note: The IPB combined obstacle overlay (IPB pp 6-12). Classes not absolute; they apply to manoeuvre in combat formation, not movement through an area (that is the road network, p 9). NO-GO does not mean impassable: speed is substantially reduced unless considerable effort is made (p 9).

classes.na: Not assessed (the bundle cannot test a criterion that applies here)

precedence.rule: A cell takes the worst class any tested criterion gives it (NO-GO > SLOW-GO > GO). Not assessed is shown where a criterion that applies locally could not be tested and no tested criterion gives NO-GO. Not classed is shown where the book gives no class and nothing else classes the cell.

movers.note: The book marks some criteria 'armoured forces only' or 'mechanized forces only'; the rest apply to every unit. Mapping from Ground Guide profiles is my proposal.

slope.directional: NO-GO and SLOW-GO are uphill along the direction of movement; GO is less than 30 degrees (written in degrees). Downhill 30 degrees or more is not classed by the book.

baselineM.note: Slope measured over 60 m (two 30 m cells) to smooth the elevation's noise.

noDirection.rule: With an all-round threat the steepest slope at the cell is treated as uphill (never understated).

relief.above: Over 400 m per km is not classed by the book (the slope test usually classes it).

windowM.note: Elevation range inside a 1 km window centred on the cell.

bua.bypass: Built-up areas that cannot be easily bypassed on both sides are NO-GO.

bypassTest.rule: Both flanks, measured square to the direction of movement within 500 m of the built-up area, are mostly water, wetland or built-up: no easy bypass.

hydrology.nogo: Rivers, streams, lakes, swamps and bogs that cannot be forded or spanned by an AVLB and are not frozen. Hard vertical banks higher than 4 ft (1.22 m) stop tanks, as will streams with velocities more than 5 ft/s (1.52 m/s) and depths greater than 4 ft (1.22 m). (As written: velocity AND depth; FM 34-130 B-6 lists them separately.)
hydrology.slow: Rivers, streams, lakes and flooded areas that can be forded or spanned in several places; velocity under 5 ft/s and depth under 4 ft. Ice 31.5 in carries tanks, 20 in howitzers.
hydrology.go: Rivers and streams that can be forded anywhere along their length or are 5 ft (1.5 m) or less wide; depth under 2 ft (0.61 m). Ice at least 4 in is GO for dismounted infantry.

avlbSpanM.src: M60 AVLB bridge 18.28 m (open sources); Pakistani in-service span not published

hydrology.notRecorded: The bundle records no water depth, current or bank height per cell: those parts are not assessed.

widthTest.rule: Width = the narrowest run of water cells through the cell (across the water, four directions, diagonals weighted, up to 40 cells) x cell size. Wider than the AVLB span: NO-GO; the bridge and ford cells themselves are crossings. A run of one cell (a line feature: canal, distributary, drain, stream) has no measurable width: not assessed.

seasonalClasses.rule: Seasonal water: depth not recorded, not assessed.

crossingClasses.rule: A bridge or ford cell is a crossing: SLOW-GO for the hydrology criterion (the load class is read on the GROTBC card).

nogo.text: Trees 6 to 8 in thick at less than 20 ft intervals.

slow.text: Trees '2 -' in thick at less than 20 ft intervals (the page drops the upper figure; FM 34-130 B-6 has 2 to 6 in).

vegetation.go: Trees less than 2 in thick or more than 20 ft apart.
vegetation.notRecorded: The bundle records no trunk thickness or spacing: not assessed for armour and mechanized forces.

negatedByRoads.rule: Roads negate vegetation unless obstacles are employed.

roads.rule: Except in open areas. NO-GO: one track per km and no hard-surface roads. SLOW-GO: one hard-surface road, or two tracks, or one road and one track per km. GO: two or more hard-surface roads per km. Slope has priority over roads and tracks.

perKm.rule: Road length inside a 1 km window divided by the window's side: the number of roads crossing a 1 km front, read as the book's 'per kilometer'.

closeClasses.note: Close country where the rule applies: trees and orchards (the book ties the rule to vegetation: 'This negates vegetation'). Built-up areas are judged by the BUA rule only.

manMade.text: Minefields, tank ditches, trees blown down and barriers (may be directional).
manMade.fromSymbols: Read from obstacle symbols on the map; ditch-cum-bund and AT ditches are not in the bundle.

waterTable.notRecorded: Not in the bundle: not assessed anywhere.

season.note: Rules from the terrain pamphlets. Whether they join the coding or stay as notes is a switch (ipb.season: coding | notes) until the user decides.

rann.text: The Rann of Kutch is impassable from June to November.

box.note: lon / lat box round the Rann.

snowClosure.text: Virtually all areas above 2500 m get blocked for 6-9 months.

months.note: Six winter months, the lower end of 6-9.

snowSlopes.text: Snow slides most dangerous on slopes over 35 degrees; deep new snow slides on slopes steeper than 25 degrees for two or three days after a fall.

applies.rule: Snow / ice class, or above 2000 m in the winter months.

corridors.levels: Mobility corridors are considered two levels down; avenues of approach one level down (IPB p 7). A viable avenue contains at least two mobility corridors.

directionToleranceDeg.rule: The threat marker's arc: half of extended.sectorDeg either side of the direction of attack.

corridors.drawing: Avenues are drawn through the area of interest regardless of boundaries, objectives, FDLs, line of advance or contact; they may start or end abruptly; never extended through ground with no corridors (IPB p 16).

hqRows.bnNote: Neither the book nor ATP 2-01.3 has a row for a Bn HQ (Coy avenues of Pl corridors): a Bn or smaller symbol reads with the Bde HQ row over its own (Bn) area, and says so.

frames.note: The area read: the HQ's frame facing the threat from the spot (frontage w, forward toward the threat fwd, behind rear), plus a lead beyond it toward the threat. Bn and Bde as the AOR scale's echelon frames; the Div frame is my proposal (no source gives one).

method.obstacles: NO-GO, SLOW-GO, not classed and not assessed ground narrow a corridor; water lines whose width is not recorded and crossings are crossed. Patches under a quarter of the corridor width squared are left out (a corridor is relatively free of obstacles).
method.ways: One least-cost field from the start edge (GO 1, SLOW-GO and not assessed 3, NO-GO never crossed, ground nearer an obstacle than half a corridor width up to 3 times dearer); the cheapest way back from each strip of the end edge (strips two spacings wide); a way within half the spacing of one kept for 60 % of its length is the same avenue.
method.viable: An avenue: two corridor widths fit side by side in the free width over 60 % of its length (book p 12: two or more corridors). One corridor width over 60 %: a lone corridor. Less: no corridor. Less than one corridor width: a narrows.
method.ranking: Until the proforma (Phase 4): 15 x share of the area run + 0.3 x GO % + 6 x corridors side by side (up to 3) - 5 per narrows - 6 per narrows under half a corridor width - 10 when stopped + 25 x cheapest cost / its cost. Higher is better going for the user of the avenue.

air.note: Air avenues of approach, LZ / DZ and AD sites (IPB s2 para 1 pp 5-6, Fig 1 p 8; IPB_Plan.md §6.4). The book gives the factors, not the figures: flight heights and LZ sizes are public US figures (basis T) until Army Aviation gives the Pakistani ones.

factors.text: Low-level and NOE flight. Sufficient air space; concealment from ground observation; easily recognised features (rivers, roads; linear features parallel to the flight best; terrain corridors give navigation and defilade); length of the flight path (shortest preferred, longer for deception); vertical obstructions (water towers, power lines). Identify LZ / DZ and AD sites giving long-range, flank or bottom shots on the air avenue.

bands.src: FM 3-04.203 Fundamentals of Flight (terrain flight modes), via open summaries
bands.note: Height above the highest obstacle (AHO). Confirm with Army Aviation.

noe.label: NOE
noe.text: Nap of the earth: as low as vegetation and obstacles permit, up to 25 ft AHO; speed and heading vary.

contour.label: Contour
contour.text: Contour: follows the ground at 25-80 ft AHO; speed fairly constant, height varies.

low.label: Low level
low.text: Low level: constant height and speed, 80-200 ft AHO.

landingPoints.src: FM 3-21.38 Pathfinder Operations ch 6 (landing point sizes), via open copies

defaultClass.note: Mi-17 class, the Army's main lift helicopter (open sources).

points.note: Landing points in one LZ; laid in a square, one point diameter apart.

slope.text: Up to 7 degrees: land. 7-15 degrees: land upslope or hover, the landing points checked on the ground. Over 15 degrees: no landing.

mountains.text: Helipads in mountains: slope 4 degrees or less for repeated use; emergency 4-10 degrees (observation / utility), 4-20 degrees (cargo).

mountainTest.rule: Elevation range within 1 km of the LZ of 200 m or more (the book's NO-GO relief, IPB p 10): the mountain rule applies.

measure.rule: Slope from the 30 m elevation over 60 m; the LZ's slope is the 90th percentile of its cells (the 30 m elevation is noisy).

approach.text: 10 to 1: an obstacle h metres high must be 10 h metres from the LZ's edge on the approach and departure; one clear direction at least, two opposite ones best (wind not known).

dz.src: DAFMAN 13-217 Drop Zone and Landing Zone Operations (personnel DZ minimum, one jumper)
dz.note: 600 x 600 yd for one jumper; a stick needs a longer DZ (the per-jumper increment is not confirmed). MW p 258: DZs scarce in mountains (level, free of rocks and trees).

clear.note: Ground classes a helicopter can land on, and those that only allow it with care (my reading of the class list; confirm).

clearShare.note: Share of a DZ that must be clear (a few small obstacles are accepted); an LZ must be clear throughout.

obstructions.note: Heights assumed where the bundle records none (metres above the ground). The book names water towers and power lines (IPB p 6).

nearM.note: An air avenue passing within this distance of a point obstruction is counted against it.

ad.src: Open figures for MANPADS (Anza Mk II, RBS 70 class) and 35 mm AD guns
ad.note: Effective range of short-range AD against helicopters; confirm with AD.

shots.text: Long-range (down the avenue), flank (beside it) and bottom (below where it crosses a ridge) shots.

rules.note: Long-range: the aircraft flies within 30 degrees of straight at the site, beyond 40 % of the range. Flank: 60-120 degrees across, within 60 % of the range. Bottom: the site 20 m or more below the avenue where the avenue crosses a crest.

priority.src: OOW1 p 27; DW pp 62-72; MW p 247
priority.text: AD priority: HQs, armour concentrations, gun areas, reserves, vital bridges (OoW I); in the desert reserves, HQs, gun areas, logistics, assault engineers, MSR bottlenecks; in mountains canalised run-ins covered from dominating features, defiles.

heliborne.text: The enemy's para and heliborne forces seize dominating ground and defile crossings, attack depth localities, HQs and reserves; OPs over likely landing areas (OoW I p 63). In mountains: hill tops, nodal points, defiles, choke points (MW p 258).

opWithinM.note: An OP for an enemy LZ: the highest own-side ground within 3 km that sees it.

cost.note: My weights for the least-cost air avenue on a 150 m grid (length 1 per cell).

rates.note: Day, night. Vehicles at night: GO with lights or passive, SLOW-GO blacked out.

interdict.rule: The decision must be made while the enemy is at least 2 hours from the TAI.

counterAttack.rule: The counter-attack must go in while the depth localities are still intact; its timing depends on the counter-attack force's mobility.

coyMin.src: IBB (counter-penetration: company counter-attack in 30 min, battalion in 1 h; OCOKA_Roadmap.md)

ownAttack.rule: Frontal attack is dangerous with small chances of success: discarded, shown for reference only. A flanking attack that chokes the enemy MSR is encouraged. Left or Right by weighing the factors.

frontDiscarded.text: The company would normally have come under effective enemy fire from the front, so this approach may be safely discarded; the ground is divided into left and right approaches.

factors.label: Route to FUP: obstacles, en interference
Fire base: cover, range, direction against the axis

weightsNote.note: Default weights are my proposal; the user sets them 0-3.

formsOfManoeuvre.src: OOW2 s6 pp 19-21; DW pp 39-42; MW p 79
formsOfManoeuvre.envelopment: Auxiliary manoeuvre draws the defender; main strength on the assailable flank. Without one, create inner flanks after a frontal penetration.
formsOfManoeuvre.doubleEnvelopment: Both flanks at once; needs adequate troops and precise co-ordination.
formsOfManoeuvre.verticalEnvelopment: By air into the rear and flanks.
formsOfManoeuvre.turningMovement: Threat to a significant objective deep in the defender's rear; needs relative mobility on an assailable flank; preceded by a fixing manoeuvre.
formsOfManoeuvre.penetration: Wedge through the front; the most commonly applied form where there are no assailable flanks; must lead to break-out; enabled by an auxiliary manoeuvre.
formsOfManoeuvre.mountains: Envelopment with frontal fixation preferred; frontal only if unavoidable, at night or in poor visibility (MW p 79).

proforma.note: Plus for advantage, minus for disadvantage; add up. The weights cannot be quantified: totals are only a rough guide (note 2).

value: access to key terrain and adjacent AAs
degree of canalization and ease of movement

weather.note: Favourable (GO) / marginal (SLOW-GO); worse than marginal is unfavourable.
